apps.name: Arch Linux (x86)
apps.sub: The operating system the Terminal's machines boot
apps.description: A real Arch Linux userland (bash, coreutils, git, kernel modules) for the x86 machines in the Terminal. Installing unpacks it into your filesystem's own / — every file of the distro becomes a normal file in Files, and the machine boots it from there over 9p. Nothing boots until this is installed: the Terminal will tell you to come here first. Uninstalling is not offered because the distro's files are woven into /; Settings → Machine can re-unpack it if it breaks.

apps.name: Arch Linux (x86-64)
apps.sub: Arch's own 64-bit build, for the x86-64 machine
apps.description: Arch Linux as Arch builds it for real 64-bit machines: the linux-lts kernel, 64-bit bash, coreutils and glibc straight from Arch's packages, and a static 64-bit git with networking and HTTPS git clone — the same tooling as the x86 build, compiled for x86_64. It needs the x86-64 machine (Settings → Machine); a 32-bit CPU cannot run it, here or anywhere. The two Arch entries share your filesystem's /, so installing this one replaces the installed (x86) userland in place — your own files stay.

apps.name: Alpine Linux (RISC-V 64)
apps.sub: Official Alpine riscv64, for the RISC-V 64 machine
apps.description: Alpine Linux as Alpine builds it for real RISC-V 64 hardware: busybox, musl, bash and Alpine's own git — a full build with working HTTPS, so git clone https://… runs natively, no helper needed. Networking comes up by itself through the emulator's fetch backend. It needs the RISC-V 64 machine (Settings → Machine); an x86 CPU cannot run it, here or anywhere. The distros share your filesystem's /, so installing this one replaces the installed Arch userland in place — your own files stay. This machine has no display: the Terminal's serial console is its console.

apps.name: NetBSD (ARM64)
apps.sub: Official NetBSD 11.0, for the ARM64 machine
apps.description: NetBSD as the NetBSD Foundation builds it for real ARM64 hardware: the official 11.0 evbarm-aarch64 release, trimmed of its X11 sets and manual pages so it fits a browser download, and boot-tested before it ships. Unlike the Linux distros it does not unpack into your filesystem's /: NetBSD boots from its own disk image in browser storage (OPFS), and its files live inside that image, in NetBSD's own FFS filesystem — Files cannot see them, and exporting your filesystem does not include them. It needs the ARM64 machine (Settings → Machine). Serial console only for now: log in as root (no password), shut down with shutdown -p now. No network on this machine yet — honestly, not “coming right up”.

apps.name: Alpine Linux (ARM32)
apps.sub: Official Alpine armv7, for the ARM32 machine
apps.description: Alpine Linux as the Alpine project builds it for 32-bit ARM: the official armv7 release — its virt kernel, initramfs, kernel modules and minirootfs userland — assembled onto an ext4 disk image and boot-tested on Dragon86's actual emulator core before it ships. It is the minimal Alpine: busybox and apk on busybox init, a few megabytes of userland, exactly what the official minirootfs contains. Unlike the Linux distros it does not unpack into your filesystem's /: it boots from its own disk image in browser storage (OPFS), and its files live inside that image, in ext4 — Files cannot see them, and exporting your filesystem does not include them. It needs the ARM32 machine (Settings → Machine). Serial console only for now: log in as root (no password), shut down with poweroff. No network on this machine yet — honestly, not “coming right up”. (It replaces the short-lived NetBSD (ARM32) entry, which the ARM32 machine's interrupt controller can never boot — any leftover NetBSD disk image is cleaned out of browser storage automatically.)

apps.name: install-wm64.sh
apps.sub: X11 + IceWM — a window manager on the machine's display
apps.publisher: Arch Linux x86_64 packages · Dragon86 pack
apps.description: A real X11 desktop for the x86-64 machine: Xorg on the machine's own display (open the Engine Viewer to see it), the IceWM window manager, and xterm — Arch's own packages, with the bochs display and evdev input kernel modules to match the installed kernel. Installing dumps /install-wm64.sh and its payload into your filesystem; the second half runs inside the machine: sh /install-wm64.sh, then startwm. Mouse and keyboard work on the Engine Viewer screen. An xterm opens with the desktop; for more, right-click the desktop (or Ctrl+Esc) for the menu, or press Ctrl+Alt+T. Needs Arch Linux (x86-64) installed and the x86_64 machine selected.

apps.name: install-netsurf.sh
apps.sub: NetSurf — a real graphical web browser, in the window manager
apps.publisher: Arch Linux x86_64 packages · Dragon86 pack
apps.description: NetSurf is a real browser engine — its own layout, CSS and image rendering — built to be light enough for exactly this kind of machine. (Chromium itself cannot run here: it needs a gigabyte of RAM and a GPU, and this is a software-emulated x86-64 with 256 MB — an install script would only pretend.) Installing dumps /install-netsurf.sh and its payload into your filesystem; inside the machine run sh /install-netsurf.sh, then start NetSurf from the IceWM menu on the Engine Viewer screen. Needs install-wm64.sh set up first, and /networking.sh for the network.

apps.name: Archimedes
apps.sub: Acorn Archimedes emulator — bring your own ROM
apps.publisher: Sarah Walker & the Arculator WASM contributors (GPL-2.0)
apps.description: A real Acorn Archimedes (ARM2/ARM3) in a window, powered by Arculator compiled to WebAssembly - graphics, sound, mouse and keyboard all work. No operating system is included: Arthur and RISC OS ROM images are still copyrighted, so the app asks you for a ROM once and keeps it in your browser's storage - it is never uploaded anywhere. The setup screen says where a legally distributed RISC OS 3.1 ROM can be found. Floppy images (.adf and friends) can be inserted from your files.

apps.name: Notes
apps.sub: Notebooks, checklists and sketches — saved in this browser
apps.description: Puter's Notes app, adapted for Dragon86: rich notes with checklists, drawings (pen and highlighter), math, PDF attachments and full-text search. Everything is stored in this browser's own database — there is no account, no sign-in, and nothing leaves your machine. From the open-source heyputer/everything collection (AGPL-3.0); the Puter cloud SDK was removed for this build.

apps.name: Whiteboard
apps.sub: Infinite canvas for sketches, diagrams and sticky notes
apps.description: Puter's Whiteboard, adapted for Dragon86: an infinite canvas with freehand drawing, shapes, connectors, sticky notes, text and image paste — with named checkpoints you can roll back to. Boards are stored in this browser's own database; no account and no cloud. From the open-source heyputer/everything collection (AGPL-3.0); the Puter cloud SDK and analytics were removed for this build, so the sharing/sign-in menu entries cannot connect to anything.

apps.name: Wiki
apps.sub: Your own wiki — linked pages, kept in this browser
apps.description: Puter's Wiki, adapted for Dragon86: linked pages with rich editing, history and search, organized into spaces. Everything lives in this browser's own database — no account, no cloud. From the open-source heyputer/everything collection (MIT); the Puter cloud SDK was removed and the app runs its upstream local mode permanently. Sharing menus act on an in-browser copy of the collaboration service only — invite links cannot reach another person.

apps.name: Photo Studio
apps.sub: Layers, brushes, masks and filters — PSD in and out
apps.description: Puter's Photo Studio, adapted for Dragon86: a layered image editor with brushes, selections, masks, adjustment layers, filters and PSD import/export. Documents are stored in this browser's own database — no account, no cloud. From the open-source heyputer/everything collection; the Puter cloud SDK was removed for this build, so collaboration/sign-in features are simply absent.

apps.name: Vector Studio
apps.sub: Pen-tool vector design with SVG import and export
apps.description: Puter's Vector Studio, adapted for Dragon86: pen and shape tools, boolean operations, gradients, typography with bundled fonts, and SVG import/export. Work is stored in this browser — no account, no cloud. From the open-source heyputer/everything collection; the Puter cloud SDK was removed for this build and the app boots straight into its local mode.

apps.name: Audio Studio
apps.sub: Record, cut and mix audio — exports MP3 and WAV
apps.description: Puter's Audio Studio, adapted for Dragon86: multitrack editing with recording, cutting, fades, effects and MP3/WAV export, all processed in the page. From the open-source heyputer/everything collection; the Puter cloud SDK was removed for this build. Note: upstream's service-worker cleanup was also removed, since on Dragon86 the service worker belongs to the OS.

apps.name: Music Studio
apps.sub: Piano-roll sequencer with built-in instruments
apps.description: Puter's Music Studio, adapted for Dragon86: a piano-roll sequencer with built-in synth instruments, drum patterns and per-track mixing. Songs and presets are stored in this browser's own database — no account, no cloud. From the open-source heyputer/everything collection; the Puter cloud SDK was removed for this build.

apps.name: Video Studio
apps.sub: Timeline video editing — media stays in this browser
apps.description: Puter's Video Studio, adapted for Dragon86: timeline editing with transitions, titles (bundled fonts), audio tracks and camera effects powered by on-device MediaPipe models — the largest app in the store because those models ship with it. Projects and media live in this browser's private storage. From the open-source heyputer/everything collection (AGPL-3.0); the Puter cloud SDK was removed and the app always uses its local library.

apps.name: 3D Studio
apps.sub: Model, sculpt and render 3D scenes in the browser
apps.description: Puter's 3D Studio, adapted for Dragon86: modeling, sculpting, materials, physics (Rapier) and path-traced rendering, offline-first by design. Scenes are stored in this browser. From the open-source heyputer/everything collection (AGPL-3.0); the only Puter feature — the cloud AI assistant — now reports itself unavailable instead of loading the SDK.

apps.name: Presentation
apps.sub: Slides with themes, charts and a presenter view
apps.description: Puter's Presentation, adapted for Dragon86: slide decks with themes, layouts, charts, drawing tools and a presenter view, plus PowerPoint import/export. Work is kept as drafts in this browser — no account, no cloud; the sign-in buttons honestly report they are unavailable in this build. From the open-source heyputer/everything collection (AGPL-3.0).

apps.name: Records
apps.sub: Tables, views and forms — a base builder in your browser
apps.description: Puter's Records, adapted for Dragon86: build bases from tables with typed fields, filtered views and forms — in the spirit of Airtable. Everything lives in this browser's own database; no account, no cloud. From the open-source heyputer/everything collection; the app runs its upstream local mode permanently.

apps.name: API Client
apps.sub: Compose and test HTTP requests, collections included
apps.description: Puter's API Client, adapted for Dragon86: compose HTTP requests, organize them into collections, use variables and inspect responses — in the spirit of Postman. Upstream's guest mode is the only mode: collections and history stay in this browser. Requests are sent only to the servers you aim them at. From the open-source heyputer/everything collection.

apps.name: CAD
apps.sub: 2D drafting with DXF/DWG import — drawings as files
apps.description: Puter's CAD, adapted for Dragon86: 2D drafting with precise tools, layers and dimensioning, opening and saving CAD/DXF/DWG files on this computer. Local recovery copies in the browser mean a reload never loses work; it is usable without any account by design. From the open-source heyputer/everything collection.

apps.name: Circuits
apps.sub: Draw and simulate electronic circuits
apps.description: Puter's Circuits, adapted for Dragon86: draw schematics from a component library and simulate them, with projects and versions kept in this browser. No account, no cloud — the app runs its own offline path. From the open-source heyputer/everything collection.

apps.name: Parametric
apps.sub: Code-driven 3D parts — OpenCascade kernel included
apps.description: Puter's Parametric, adapted for Dragon86: model 3D parts with code, powered by the replicad/OpenCascade geometry kernel running locally (the 22 MB of WebAssembly ships with the app). Parts stay in this browser; export produces files. From the open-source heyputer/everything collection (AGPL-3.0).

apps.name: Building Design
apps.sub: Floor plans and building layouts — projects as files
apps.description: Puter's Building Design, adapted for Dragon86: draw floor plans with walls, doors, windows and measurements, saving projects as files on this computer with browser-side recovery copies. Usable without any account by design. From the open-source heyputer/everything collection (AGPL-3.0).

apps.name: EmulatorJS
apps.sub: Play games from your own files
apps.description: EmulatorJS frontend for user-selected game files. Supports a range of systems, including PS1, with no ROMs or BIOS bundled. Runtime/core files load from the EmulatorJS CDN; an internet connection is required.

apps.name: PlayStation (PS1)
apps.sub: EmulatorJS PS1 core · no COI required
apps.description: PlayStation emulation using EmulatorJS and its pcsx_rearmed core. Select your own disc image (CHD/PBP recommended); no games or BIOS are bundled. The core runs single-threaded and does not require cross-origin isolation. EmulatorJS runtime files load from its CDN.

apps.name: Tasks
apps.sub: Personal and shared to-do lists
apps.description: Puter Tasks: task lists, reminders, recurring tasks, calendar integration, and cross-device sync. Uses Puter.js and requires an internet connection and Puter account for cloud features.

apps.name: Contacts
apps.sub: A private address book in your Puter cloud
apps.description: Puter Contacts: searchable address book with vCard import/export, tags, and cross-device cloud sync. Uses Puter.js and requires an internet connection and Puter account.

apps.name: Snake
apps.sub: The classic, with a score and a speed curve
apps.description: Grid-based snake with a score, a speed curve, and swipe controls for phones. Arrow keys or WASD on a keyboard. The board waits for your first key or tap, and the game pauses itself when the window loses focus. No scoreboard, no accounts, no pop-ups.

apps.name: Sudoku
apps.sub: Classic sudoku with hints, notes and stats — all local
apps.description: Puter's Sudoku, adapted for Dragon86: four difficulties, pencil notes, hints, mistake checking and personal best times. Puzzles in progress and stats are kept in this browser — no account, no cloud. From the open-source heyputer/everything collection (MIT); the Puter cloud SDK was removed for this build, so the app simply never shows its sign-in button.

apps.name: Chess
apps.sub: Play the computer or a friend at this keyboard
apps.description: Puter's Chess, adapted for Dragon86: play against the computer at several strengths or two players at one keyboard, with move history, undo and board themes. Settings and the game in progress stay in this browser. From the open-source heyputer/everything collection (MIT); online multiplayer needed Puter's servers, so in this build the Online menu honestly says it is unavailable.

apps.name: Checkers
apps.sub: Draughts against the computer or a friend — all local
apps.description: Puter's Checkers, adapted for Dragon86: play draughts against the computer or two players at one keyboard, with undo and move history. Settings and the game in progress stay in this browser. From the open-source heyputer/everything collection (MIT); online multiplayer needed Puter's servers, so in this build the Online menu honestly says it is unavailable.

apps.name: Backgammon
apps.sub: Backgammon with doubling cube, vs computer or hotseat
apps.description: Puter's Backgammon, adapted for Dragon86: full rules including the doubling cube, against the computer or two players at one keyboard. Settings and the game in progress stay in this browser. From the open-source heyputer/everything collection (MIT); online multiplayer needed Puter's servers, so in this build the Online menu honestly says it is unavailable.

apps.name: Solitaire
apps.sub: Klondike and friends — saves and stats in this browser
apps.description: Puter's Solitaire, adapted for Dragon86: Klondike and more modes with drag-and-drop, undo, auto-complete and per-mode stats. Saves and statistics live in this browser. From the open-source heyputer/everything collection (MIT); the Puter cloud SDK and its optional sync were removed for this build, and its own offline service worker is disabled because Dragon86 already serves apps through one.

apps.name: Calculator
apps.sub: Arithmetic that keeps working offline
apps.description: A pocket calculator: add, subtract, multiply and divide, plus percent, sign flip and clear. Tap the buttons or use the number keys, Enter for equals and Escape to clear. It keeps twelve digits on screen, then switches to precision notation. Deliberately dull — a calculator that wants to be clever is a calculator that lies.

apps.name: Monaco Editor
apps.sub: The editor behind VS Code, for your own files
apps.description: A full code editor with syntax highlighting for dozens of languages, multi-cursor editing and bracket matching. It reads and writes the same filesystem as Files, so saving a script here is the same as saving it anywhere else. Not installed by default: the Text Editor is always there, and this is for when you want the heavy one. Typefaces and the whole editor are served from the OS itself, with nothing fetched from a CDN.

apps.name: GUST
apps.sub: Web proxy that runs from your own files
apps.description: A single-file web proxy with its fonts and icons vendored alongside it, so nothing is fetched from a CDN. In the guest under v86 the same page uses the guest's curl; in the browser it uses the Wisp server you give it in the page's own settings.

apps.name: Sandstone
apps.sub: Sandboxed-iframe web proxy
apps.description: Runs proxied pages inside a sandboxed iframe, with its own home page and stylesheet shipped in the folder. No service worker, no external assets.

apps.name: CheerpJ
apps.sub: Run .jar files — Java in the browser
apps.publisher: Dragon Gaming Platforms (runtime by Leaning Technologies)
apps.description: CheerpJ is a full Java runtime in WebAssembly: pick a .jar from your files and it runs, unmodified. Programs with a Swing or AWT interface get their own display inside the window; console programs print underneath it. Once installed it offers to open .jar files, so double-clicking one in Files runs it here. The Java runtime itself is downloaded from Leaning Technologies' CDN on first use — it is far too large to vendor — so the first run needs a network connection.

apps.name: vAmigaWeb
apps.sub: Full AGA Amiga emulator · web only
apps.description: A full AGA Amiga emulator that runs on the web, with RetroShell and snapshots. Opens on the upstream site in a separate tab. It is not a Dragon86 Terminal engine: there is no Dragon86 9P mount, and Dragon86 does not bundle ROMs or software.

apps.name: vAmiga
apps.sub: 68k Amiga · macOS project
apps.description: The upstream vAmiga 500/1000/2000 emulator project for macOS. This is a source-project listing, not a browser build or a Dragon86 Terminal engine; it does not mount Dragon86's 9P share.

apps.name: Basilisk II
apps.sub: 68k Macintosh emulator · native project
apps.description: Basilisk II is the 68k Macintosh emulator in the macemu project. This listing opens its upstream source repository; it is not a browser-ready build or a Dragon86 Terminal engine, and no 9P file sharing is provided.

apps.name: Mini vMac
apps.sub: Compact 68k Macintosh emulator · project links
apps.description: Mini vMac is a compact classic Macintosh emulator. The project site provides Mini vMac information and builds; the source link is the supplied iOS port. Neither is a Dragon86 9P-backed Terminal engine, and Dragon86 does not bundle ROMs or disk images.

apps.name: SheepShaver
apps.sub: PowerPC Macintosh emulator · native project
apps.description: SheepShaver is the PowerPC Macintosh emulator in the macemu project. This listing opens the upstream source repository; it is not a browser-ready build or a Dragon86 Terminal engine, and no 9P file sharing is provided.

apps.name: DingusPPC
apps.sub: Experimental PowerPC emulator · source project
apps.description: DingusPPC is an experimental PowerPC emulator project. The App Store entry links to its upstream source; it is not a browser engine integrated with Dragon86 and has no Dragon86 9P mount.

apps.name: PearPC
apps.sub: PowerPC platform emulator · source project
apps.description: PearPC is a PowerPC platform emulator for running PowerPC operating systems. The supplied pearpc/pearpc GitHub URL was not found; this entry uses the verified sebastianbiallas/pearpc repository and the project site. It is a source-project link, not a browser engine or a Dragon86 9P integration.

apps.name: Infinite Mac
apps.sub: Classic 68k and PowerPC Macs in the browser
apps.description: Launch the Infinite Mac browser experience in a separate tab, or inspect its source. This upstream hosted service is not connected to Dragon86's filesystem and does not mount its 9P share. Dragon86 does not bundle system ROMs or disk images.

apps.name: jsbeeb
apps.sub: BBC Micro emulator · browser version
apps.description: Launch the JavaScript BBC Micro emulator on its upstream site, or inspect the source. It runs outside Dragon86 and is not connected to Dragon86's 9P filesystem share.

apps.name: Apple IIjs
apps.sub: Apple II emulator · browser project
apps.description: Open the Apple IIjs hosted emulator or its source repository in a separate tab. This external page is not mounted to Dragon86's filesystem and does not provide a Dragon86 9P guest share.

apps.name: WebMSX
apps.sub: MSX emulator · browser version
apps.description: Launch the upstream WebMSX online emulator or inspect its source. It runs in its own tab; Dragon86 does not embed it, install files into it, or mount the OS filesystem over 9P.

apps.name: JSSpeccy 3
apps.sub: ZX Spectrum emulator · browser version
apps.description: Launch the upstream JSSpeccy 3 browser emulator or inspect its source. It runs outside Dragon86 and has no Dragon86 9P filesystem mount.

apps.name: PDP-11/70 Emulator
apps.sub: PDP-11/70 · verified project alternative
apps.description: The supplied dcheney/pdp11 GitHub URL was not found. This links to a verifiable PDP-11/70 emulator project and its source; the project documents Linux and Raspberry Pi targets, not a browser build. It is an informational project listing, not a Dragon86 engine or 9P integration.
